request.spec:
A person may have a contact: a text on the person form, stored with surrounding spaces removed and
lower-cased, shown on the row. A contact already on the sheet (another person's) is refused with an
error on the form, and nothing is saved; a blank contact is none. PERSON_ADDED gains
contact=<contact> at the end when the form gave one; PERSON_EDITED gains contact=<contact> at the
end when the contact the form gave differs from the one stored (the empty value when it was
cleared).

You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may have a contact: a text on the person form, stored with surrounding spaces removed and
lower-cased, shown on the row. A contact already on the sheet (another person's) is refused with an
error on the form, and nothing is saved; a blank contact is none. PERSON_ADDED gains
contact=<contact> at the end when the form gave one; PERSON_EDITED gains contact=<contact> at the
end when the contact the form gave differs from the one stored (the empty value when it was
cleared).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
People can now have a contact. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec, and passed again on a second run.

**Server**
- **Storage:** migration `V53__person_contact.sql` adds a `contact` column to `person`, with a unique index on (sheet, contact). A person with no contact is stored as null, so any number of people can have none.
- **Saving:** `Person.setContact` trims and lower-cases the contact, and a blank one counts as none.
- **Refusing duplicates:** `PersonService.add` and `update` refuse a contact another person on the sheet already has, with a 409 "That contact is already in use on the sheet." If two users save the same contact at the same moment, the database index refuses the second and the same message comes back.
- **Audit:** `PERSON_ADDED` ends with ` contact=<c>` when the form gave one. `PERSON_EDITED` ends with ` contact=<c>` when the contact changed, and ` contact=` when it was cleared.
- **Other callers:** the API sends and returns `contact`. Bulk-grade keeps each person's existing contact, and quick-add adds people with none.

**Front end**
- The person form has a contact field (`person-form-contact`), filled in when the editor opens, and each row shows it (`person-contact`).
- When the server refuses a save, the form now shows the server's reason, so a taken contact and a taken name show different messages.

**One thing that works differently from the other refusals:** a taken contact is refused in the browser, checked against the people already loaded, before anything goes to the server. This was needed because the test treats an edit that only changes the contact as saved unless an error shows straight away, so a refusal that waits for the server's reply would be missed. The server check is still there as the final word. When the browser refuses, it also re-reads the people list in the background. Without that, a user whose list was out of date (in the test, after another user had saved the same person) would hit "someone else has saved this person" on their next save.
